challenge.method: Tested two distributions to another recipient with no upstream NOTICE file: an unmodified Object-form copy of the Work and a modified Derivative Work in Source form. Compared giving the recipient an actual license copy with giving only an SPDX label in a source header. Checked the Appendix and the remainder of Section 4 for an alternative to 4(a).
challenge.results: Both distributions meet the preamble's conditions for applying 4(a). Giving the recipient the license text fulfills the copy requirement in each case. An SPDX label alone identifies the license but omits its terms. Absence of upstream NOTICE removes the 4(d) trigger and leaves 4(a) applicable. The Appendix tells an author how to apply the license to a work. It gives no exception to the recipient-copy condition. The closing paragraph of Section 4 permits additional or different terms subject to continued compliance for the Work. No contradictory text was found.

limitations: The finding concerns the printed redistribution condition. Delivery channel, filename, language alternatives, other distribution conditions, and any work-specific exception or additional agreement are outside its scope.

reasoning: Section 4 permits reproduction and distribution in any medium, with or without modifications, in Source or Object form, provided the listed conditions are met. Section 4(a) expressly requires giving any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works “a copy of this License.” Section 1 defines the License as the terms in Sections 1 through 9. It defines the Work as the work of authorship made available under the License as indicated by an included or attached copyright notice. Source is the preferred form for making modifications. Object is a form resulting from mechanical transformation or translation of Source.
